slides.title: TeleConsole
slides.subtitle: Waiting queue and thesis-title defense
slides.notes: Use the official thesis title exactly as shown. This is a rehearsal supplement, not a replacement for the institution's full methodology/results deck. slides.title: The title describes the engineering scope
rows: Verified direct entry or clinician admission
slides.bottom: Secure is a design objective with tested controls and disclosed gaps
slides.notes: We did not invent WebRTC, an SFU or a clinical diagnostic model. We built the application workflow connecting admission, ownership, media, consent and documentation. Explain Secure with the actual server controls and specific test scope. Do not claim certification, zero vulnerabilities or measured clinical outcome improvement. The title does not expand the dental study into every medical specialty. Sources: manuscript title; docs/access-control.md; lib/invitations/admission-policy.ts; lib/services/consultation-finalization/summary-generator.ts.

slides.title: The waiting queue supports clinician admission
slides.lead: A valid invitation can reach the wrong person
rows: Reviews identity provenance and admits a row
Checks ownership and current invitation state
slides.bottom: Oldest-arrival display leaves the admission decision with the doctor
slides.notes: A forwarded link does not prove identity. The worklist lets the owning clinician review unverified visitors. Typed email, IP and browser resemblance cannot grant verified access. The list sorts oldest joinedAt first, but a doctor can choose another row. This is not an automatic FIFO scheduler or an emergency-triage algorithm. Sources: lib/services/invitation-access/invitation-access-core.ts, sortWaitingByJoinedAt and admitWaitingEntry; lib/invitations/validate-service.ts.

slides.title: Patient admission flow
slides.bottom: Current invitation, consent and usage checks still apply to both paths
slides.notes: Walk the diagram from the signed invitation to server validation. A qualifying non-anonymous authenticated account with provider-verified email on the allowlist can receive direct access. Other accepted visitors wait for a clinician decision. The doctor issues no grant by merely changing UI state; the backend verifies current ownership and invitation/row state. Current capacity pre-check can refuse validation before the direct/reconnect branch as well. Admission then leads to visible preflight and a separate Join action, not proof of live media. Sources: lib/invitations/validate-service.ts; lib/services/invitation-access/invitation-access-core.ts.

slides.title: Queue, media and encounter states
rows: The visitor awaits an admission decision
slides.bottom: Each state answers a different question
slides.notes: Do not call the admitted count a reliable attendance count. The patient may never click Join, may lose device permission or may disconnect. A connection does not by itself establish correct clinical evidence or completion. Queue departure/removal no longer closes a clinical record selected only by reusable room name. The waiting branch also mounts a hidden RoomShell preflight path. Its existence/source comment does not prove actual waiting media sharing or zero device work. Review that path in staging. Sources: WaitingRoomPanel.tsx; app/invite/[token]/page.tsx; RoomShell.tsx; invitation-access-core.ts.

slides.title: The default waiting target
slides.label: waiting visitors per invitation by default
rows: Positive finite input is clamped to at most 100
Waiting rows for this invitation and room
Maximum simultaneous video calls remains unmeasured
slides.bottom: Concurrent arrivals can exceed the configured target
slides.notes: Ten is a configuration target, not an experiment. Admitted participants are another state and several invitations may use the same room. The hard atomic waiting-capacity guarantee is not passed. The next slide shows a reproducible local counterexample. Do not answer a maximum media-capacity question with ten, one hundred or the provider's endpoint allowance. Sources: app/api/invite/create/route.ts; lib/invitations/validate-service.ts; evidence/queue-title-2026-11-25/source-audit.json.

slides.title: The capacity check can race
slides.bottom: Local synthetic interleaving only. Hard atomic capacity guarantee: NOT PASSED
slides.notes: Start with nine waiting rows and a target of ten. Both distinct visitors run the actual capacity pre-check before either reservation, so both see room for a visitor. The real reservation function serializes invitation-use updates but does not re-count or reserve waiting capacity. Both commit and the synthetic adapter ends at eleven. This is one possible interleaving, not a cloud test, production incident or maximum overshoot bound. No application fix ships in this documentation request. A later reviewed fix needs atomic slot accounting and lifecycle release/reconnect tests. Source: scripts/thesis/audit-queue-contract.mjs and its report.

slides.title: Two refresh paths
rows: Immediate check, then about every 3 seconds
One browser runtime and matching request scope
slides.bottom: Intervals describe implementation timing, not a response-time guarantee
slides.notes: The patient uses polling with an in-flight guard and cleanup. The doctor receives Firestore change invalidations, then re-queries the authenticated filtered API. Hidden doctor tabs pause periodic reconciliation, but do not generalize this behavior to every patient loop. Separate tabs/devices/scopes can issue their own traffic. Network, browser throttling and failures affect actual latency. The old manuscript's patient Firestore-listener statement is corrected. Sources: app/invite/[token]/page.tsx; hooks/useWaitingQueue.ts; lib/waiting-room/waiting-queue-coordinator.ts.

slides.title: A queue-load planning example
slides.lead: 10 waiting pages at a nominal 3-second interval
slides.label: admission HTTP checks per minute
slides.bottom: Database reads, media endpoints and AI requests require separate measurement
slides.notes: The arithmetic is ten times sixty divided by three. It excludes browser throttling, slow-request overlap protection and other requests. It is not a measured Firestore read total. Authorization, invitation lookups, counters and listener updates add work. Doctor periodic reconciliation is roughly four per minute per active scope, plus invalidations/actions. activeOnly filters the output but some doctor queries still read historical rows first. More storage does not remove repeated read cost. Source: queue client/coordinator and invitation-access-core.ts; derived planning arithmetic.

slides.title: Current controls and release gates
rows: Server ownership, signed credentials and current-state checks
Waiting capacity is not atomically reserved
Complete unique-visit replay binding remains unresolved
Review hidden preflight, stale/error behavior and bounded reads
slides.bottom: A Ready deployment does not establish every security or load criterion
slides.notes: Use the current release boundaries honestly. Previous CI/regression passes establish specific tested properties. They do not eliminate the newly reproduced capacity gap or the earlier visit-generation/replay gap. Doctor role approval is separate from Google authentication. Real-clinic release also needs configured policies, retention/restore, provider agreements and monitoring. The supplied deployment screen says Ready; we do not use that as authenticated production acceptance. Sources: docs/testing/verification-status.md; docs/access-control.md; queue source audit.

slides.title: A short synthetic demonstration
steps: 1  Show a valid guest invitation entering the waiting view
3  Admit the selected row as the owning doctor
4  Show visible preflight, then the connected call
5  Compare admission state with actual media presence
slides.bottom: A separate verified-allowlist example demonstrates the direct-entry exception
slides.notes: Prepare synthetic accounts in separate browser profiles. Do not reveal raw tokens or patient information. Preflight actual device behavior beforehand, especially the hidden waiting mount. Do not claim the demonstration measures concurrency, proves every replay case, or guarantees a waiting time. Run the direct-entry exception separately so the panel does not conclude every patient must wait. If the service fails, show the truthful error/retry state instead of bypassing admission. No live capture or paid AI load was performed to author these slides.

slides.title: Three writers, one explanation
rows: Title, study scope and evidence boundaries
Admission flow, ownership and state distinctions
Capacity target, refresh arithmetic and limitations
slides.bottom: Each writer should answer one question outside their main section
slides.notes: For a five-minute explanation: writer one takes about one minute, writer two about two minutes, writer three about one minute, and use the last minute for cross-questions. Flexible access does not mean unrestricted doctor sign-up. Secure is qualified by controls and gaps. Ten waiting is not a tested video maximum. For a full rehearsal use the comprehensive guide and all slides for twelve to fifteen minutes with pauses. Sources: waiting-queue-and-title-defense.md and panel-questions-and-answers.md.

slides.title: Panel answers to rehearse
rows: A forwarded link does not establish patient identity
Oldest-first display, with manual clinician choice
It means the server granted access
Can you guarantee a cap of ten?
No. The current capacity check can race
slides.bottom: State the rule, its reason, the evidence and the limitation
slides.notes: Have teammates answer these without reading. Add follow-ups: what does the transaction protect; is eleven the maximum overshoot; can several invitations share a room; can Google grant doctor privileges; why does a spinner not establish real-time database success? Use the thirty-two-question panel PDF for fuller responses. Avoid invented rebuttals or a guaranteed pass claim. Source: panel-questions-and-answers.md.
